UNIFORM FIDUCIARY INCOME AND PRINCIPAL ACT — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan Alex Lee · The Jordan Alex Lee Revocable Living Trust

BACKGROUND INFORMATION — UNIFORM FIDUCIARY INCOME AND PRINCIPAL ACT
I, Jordan Alex Lee, am serving, or have been asked to serve, as trustee of The Jordan Alex Lee Revocable Living Trust, executed March 14, 2020. This information sheet describes California's Uniform Fiduciary Income and Principal Act (Probate Code §§ 16320-16383), the statute that governs how a trustee allocates receipts and disbursements between principal and income when the terms of a trust do not otherwise say, and the trustee's statutory powers to adjust between principal and income or to convert the trust to a unitrust in administering it impartially between an income beneficiary and a remainder beneficiary. This information sheet is educational only. It does not evaluate, approve, or ratify any specific allocation, adjustment, unitrust conversion, or other administration decision made or proposed for The Jordan Alex Lee Revocable Living Trust; does not determine whether The Jordan Alex Lee Revocable Living Trust's own terms displace any default rule described in this document; and is not legal or tax advice. Preparing, reviewing, or signing this information sheet does not itself satisfy, waive, or discharge any duty Jordan Alex Lee owes as trustee of The Jordan Alex Lee Revocable Living Trust.

WHAT THE UNIFORM FIDUCIARY INCOME AND PRINCIPAL ACT IS AND WHEN IT APPLIES
California Probate Code § 16320 states that the chapter beginning at that section "shall be known, and may be cited, as the Uniform Fiduciary Income and Principal Act." This chapter, commonly abbreviated UFIPA, replaced California's former Uniform Principal and Income Act effective January 1, 2024. Probate Code § 16322 sets the chapter's scope: except as otherwise provided in the terms of a trust or the chapter itself, it applies to a trust or an estate, and to a life estate or other term interest in which the interest of one or more persons will be succeeded by the interest of one or more other persons. The chapter governs a fiduciary's allocation of what it receives and what it pays out as between principal (generally, the assets held for eventual distribution to a remainder beneficiary) and income (generally, the current return on those assets available for a current income beneficiary), and the fiduciary's related powers to depart from the statute's default allocations.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "This section shall be known, and may be cited, as the Uniform Fiduciary Income and Principal Act."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 16320 (California Legislative Information text), the short title of the Uniform Fiduciary Income and Principal Act (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=16320.)
  "Except as otherwise provided in the terms of a trust or this chapter, this chapter applies to the following: (a) A trust or an estate. (b) A life estate or other term interest in which the interest of one or more persons will be succeeded by the interest of one or more other persons."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 16322 (California Legislative Information text), the chapter's scope of application to trusts, estates, and life estates or other term interests (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=16322.)
  Known gap: This document describes only the current UFIPA text as codified beginning January 1, 2024 (Stats. 2023, Ch. 28, Sec. 2 (SB 522)); it does not address transition or savings-clause questions for a trust's or estate's receipts, disbursements, or other administration events that occurred before that effective date, which may still be governed by the former Uniform Principal and Income Act's different text. It also does not determine, for any specific arrangement, whether that arrangement is in fact a trust, an estate, or a § 16322(b) "life estate or other term interest" -- that classification is fact-specific and is not resolved here.

THE STATUTE'S DEFAULT-RULE STATUS: TRUST TERMS AND FIDUCIARY DISCRETION CONTROL FIRST
UFIPA's allocation rules are defaults, not mandates that override a trust's own terms. Probate Code § 16325(a) provides that in making an allocation or determination, or exercising discretion, under the chapter: a fiduciary shall act in good faith, based on what is fair and reasonable to all beneficiaries; a fiduciary shall administer a trust or decedent's estate in accordance with the trust or the will, even if there is a different provision in the chapter; a fiduciary may administer a trust or decedent's estate by exercising a discretionary power of administration given by the trust or will, even if the exercise produces a result different from what the chapter would require or permit, without any inference of impropriety arising from that fact alone; and a fiduciary shall administer a trust or decedent's estate in accordance with the chapter only if the trust or will does not contain a different provision and does not give the fiduciary a discretionary power of administration. In other words, The Jordan Alex Lee Revocable Living Trust's own express terms, and any discretionary administration power The Jordan Alex Lee Revocable Living Trust grants Jordan Alex Lee, take priority over UFIPA's statutory default rules; the statute fills gaps the trust instrument leaves open.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(a) In making an allocation or determination or exercising discretion under this chapter, all of the following apply: (1) A fiduciary shall act in good faith, based on what is fair and reasonable to all beneficiaries. (2) A fiduciary shall administer a trust or decedent’s estate in accordance with the trust or the will, even if there is a different provision in this chapter. (3) A fiduciary may administer a trust or decedent’s estate by the exercise of a discretionary power of administration given to the fiduciary by the trust or the will, even if the exercise of the power produces a result different from a result required or permitted by this chapter, and no inference that the fiduciary has improperly exercised the discretion arises from the fact that the fiduciary has made an allocation contrary to a provision of this chapter. (4) A fiduciary shall administer a trust or decedent’s estate in accordance with this chapter if the trust or the will does not contain a different provision or does not give the fiduciary a discretionary power of administration."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 16325(a) (California Legislative Information text), trust terms and discretionary administration power controlling over the chapter's default rules (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=16325.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes only subdivision (a) of § 16325. The same section separately provides, in subdivision (b), a presumption that a fiduciary's allocation, determination, or exercise of discretion is fair and reasonable to all beneficiaries, and in subdivisions (c) through (e), a residual catch-all principal allocation and a list of factors relevant to certain other statutory powers -- none of that additional text is quoted or applied here. This document does not read or interpret any particular trust's actual governing instrument to determine whether, or to what extent, its terms displace a specific default rule described elsewhere in this document.

THE TRUSTEE'S STATUTORY POWER TO ADJUST BETWEEN INCOME AND PRINCIPAL
UFIPA gives a trustee a distinct statutory tool for administering a trust impartially between income and remainder beneficiaries: the power to adjust. Probate Code § 16327(a) provides that except as otherwise provided in the terms of a trust or the section itself, "a fiduciary, in a record, without court approval, may adjust between income and principal if the fiduciary determines the exercise of the power to adjust will assist the fiduciary in administering the trust or estate impartially." Under § 16327(b), the statute does not create a duty to exercise or even consider the power to adjust, or to inform a beneficiary about it, and under § 16327(c), a fiduciary that in good faith exercises or fails to exercise the power is not liable to a person affected by that choice.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Except as otherwise provided in the terms of a trust or this section, a fiduciary, in a record, without court approval, may adjust between income and principal if the fiduciary determines the exercise of the power to adjust will assist the fiduciary in administering the trust or estate impartially."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 16327(a) (California Legislative Information text), the trustee's power to adjust between income and principal without court approval (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=16327.)
  "(b) This section does not create a duty to exercise or consider the power to adjust under subdivision (a) or to inform a beneficiary about the applicability of this section. (c) A fiduciary that in good faith exercises or fails to exercise the power to adjust under subdivision (a) is not liable to a person affected by the exercise or failure to exercise."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 16327(b)-(c) (California Legislative Information text), no duty to exercise or consider the power to adjust, and no liability for a good-faith choice either way (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=16327.)
  Known gap: Subdivision (e) of § 16327 -- not quoted in this clause -- lists nine specific circumstances in which the power to adjust may not be exercised at all, including trusts that qualify for certain special tax benefits, interests payable as a fixed annuity or fixed fraction, permanent charitable set-asides, arrangements that would trigger federal income, estate, or gift tax consequences, a fiduciary who is not an "independent person," certain irrevocable trusts with a settlor income interest tied to public benefit eligibility, and a trust that is already a unitrust under Article 3. This document does not apply those restrictions, or the cofiduciary and delegation rules in subdivisions (f) through (h), to any specific trust or any specific adjustment; whether the power to adjust is available for a particular trust and a particular adjustment is not determined here.

THE TRUSTEE'S POWER TO CONVERT BETWEEN AN INCOME TRUST AND A UNITRUST
Separate from the power to adjust, UFIPA gives a trustee a power to change how a trust calculates the amount available to an income beneficiary in the first place. Probate Code § 16332(a) provides that a fiduciary, without court approval, by complying with the section's other requirements, may convert an income trust to a unitrust (so that net income becomes a fixed unitrust amount, typically a percentage of trust value, rather than actual income received), change the percentage or method used to calculate an existing unitrust amount, or convert a unitrust back to an income trust. Under § 16332(b), a fiduciary may take that action only if the fiduciary determines it will assist in administering the trust impartially, sends notice describing and proposing the action as required by § 16333, and no beneficiary objects within the applicable period; if a beneficiary does object, § 16332(c) allows the fiduciary or a beneficiary to ask the court to permit, modify, or prevent the proposed action.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(a) A fiduciary, without court approval, by complying with subdivisions (b) and (f), may do any of the following: (1) Convert an income trust to a unitrust if the fiduciary creates in a record a unitrust plan for the trust providing for both of the following: (A) That in administering the trust, the net income of the trust will be a unitrust amount rather than net income determined without regard to this article. (B) The percentage and method used to calculate the unitrust amount. (2) Change the percentage or method used to calculate a unitrust amount for a unitrust if the fiduciary implements in a record a unitrust plan or an amendment or replacement of a unitrust plan providing changes in the percentage or method used to calculate the unitrust amount. (3) Convert a unitrust to an income trust if the fiduciary implements in a record a determination that, in administering the trust, the net income of the trust will be net income determined without regard to this article rather than a unitrust amount."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 16332(a) (California Legislative Information text), the fiduciary's power, without court approval, to convert an income trust to a unitrust, change a unitrust's calculation, or convert a unitrust back to an income trust (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=16332.)
  "(b) A fiduciary may take an action under subdivision (a) if all of the following conditions are met: (1) The fiduciary determines that the action will assist the fiduciary to administer a trust impartially. (2) The fiduciary sends a notice in a record, in the manner required by Section 16333, describing and proposing to take the action. (3) No beneficiary objects to the proposed action in a writing delivered to the trustee within the period prescribed by subdivision (d) of Section 16502. (c) If a fiduciary receives, on or before the date stated in the notice under Section 16333, an objection in a record to a proposed action, the fiduciary or a beneficiary may request the court to have the proposed action taken as proposed, taken with modifications, or prevented."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 16332(b)-(c) (California Legislative Information text), conditions for taking the action -- an impartiality determination, notice, and the consequence of a beneficiary's objection (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=16332.)
  Known gap: This clause does not describe the detailed content requirements for a unitrust plan under §§ 16334-16338 (for example, the unitrust rate, the valuation method, or default provisions that apply if the plan is silent), nor the categories of trusts Probate Code § 16331(b) excludes from Article 3 entirely -- certain trusts tied to specific Internal Revenue Code provisions (26 U.S.C. §§ 170(f)(2)(B), 642(c)(5), 664(d), 2702(a)(3)(A)(ii)-(iii), or 2702(b)), such as certain charitable remainder and split-interest trusts. Whether a particular trust is eligible for unitrust conversion under this article, and what a specific unitrust plan for that trust should provide, is not addressed here.

REQUIRED NOTICE CONTENTS AND THE MINIMUM 30-DAY OBJECTION WINDOW
The notice a fiduciary must send before converting an income trust to a unitrust, changing a unitrust's calculation, or converting a unitrust back to an income trust has statutorily required contents. Probate Code § 16333 lists what the notice must include: the proposed action; for a conversion to a unitrust, a copy of the adopted unitrust plan; for a change in calculation, a copy of the amended or replacement plan; a statement that the recipient may object by stating the basis for the objection and delivering it to the fiduciary; the fiduciary's name and contact information; and the name and contact information of a person who can be contacted for more information. On timing, § 16333(e) requires the notice to state "[t]he date by which an objection under subdivision (d) shall be received by the fiduciary, which shall be at least 30 days after the date the notice is sent."

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "A notice required by paragraph (2) of subdivision (b) of Section 16332 shall be sent as required by Chapter 5 (commencing with Section 16500), including notice to a beneficiary who is a minor and to the minor’s guardian, if any, and shall include all of the following: (a) The action proposed under paragraph (2) of subdivision (b) of Section 16332. (b) For a conversion of an income trust to a unitrust, a copy of the unitrust plan adopted under paragraph (1) of subdivision (a) of Section 16332. (c) For a change in the percentage or method used to calculate the unitrust amount, a copy of the unitrust plan or amendment or replacement of the unitrust plan adopted under paragraph (2) of subdivision (a) of Section 16332. (d) A statement that the person to which the notice is sent may object to the proposed action by stating in a record the basis for the objection and sending or delivering the record to the fiduciary. (e) The date by which an objection under subdivision (d) shall be received by the fiduciary, which shall be at least 30 days after the date the notice is sent."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 16333 (California Legislative Information text), the required contents of the notice of a proposed unitrust conversion or calculation change (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=16333.)
  Known gap: This clause describes only the content requirements listed directly in § 16333; it does not describe the separate service mechanics referenced in that section -- § 16333 requires notice to be sent "as required by Chapter 5 (commencing with Section 16500), including notice to a beneficiary who is a minor and to the minor's guardian, if any" -- and this document does not quote or apply that Chapter 5 notice-service statute. Thirty days is a statutory floor, not a fixed deadline: a fiduciary may set a longer objection period, and this clause does not determine what objection period, if any, applies to a specific notice already sent for any particular trust.

DEFAULT ALLOCATION OF MONEY RECEIVED FROM A CORPORATION, LLC, OR SIMILAR ENTITY
UFIPA sets a default rule for one of the most common receipts a trustee handles: a distribution from an entity in which the trust owns an interest, such as a corporation, partnership, limited liability company, regulated investment company, or real estate investment trust. Probate Code § 16340(c) provides the baseline: "Except as otherwise provided in paragraphs (2) to (4), inclusive, of subdivision (d), a fiduciary shall allocate money received in an entity distribution to income." Subdivision (d) then carves out categories that instead go to principal: property received that is not money; money received in exchange for part or all of the fiduciary's interest to the extent the distribution reduces that interest relative to other owners; money the fiduciary determines or estimates is a "capital distribution" (a return of capital or a total or partial liquidating distribution); and money from a regulated investment company or real estate investment trust that is a capital gain dividend, or comparably treated, for federal income tax purposes.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Except as otherwise provided in paragraphs (2) to (4), inclusive, of subdivision (d), a fiduciary shall allocate money received in an entity distribution to income."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 16340(c) (California Legislative Information text), the default rule allocating money received in an entity distribution to income (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=16340.)
  "A fiduciary shall allocate to principal all of the following: (1) Property received in an entity distribution that is not money. (2) Money received in an entity distribution in an exchange for part or all of the fiduciary’s interest in the entity, to the extent the entity distribution reduces the fiduciary’s interest in the entity relative to the interests of other persons that own or hold interests in the entity. (3) Money received in an entity distribution that the fiduciary determines or estimates is a capital distribution. (4) Money received in an entity distribution from an entity that is a regulated investment company or real estate investment trust if the money received is a capital gain dividend for federal income tax purposes. (5) Money received in an entity distribution that is treated, for federal income purposes, comparably to the treatment described in paragraph (4)."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 16340(d) (California Legislative Information text), the categories of entity distributions allocated to principal instead (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=16340.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes only the baseline income/principal split in subdivisions (c) and (d); it does not quote or apply subdivisions (e) through (i), which set out the safe harbors, a 20%-of-fair-market-value threshold, and a multi-factor test a fiduciary may use to determine or estimate whether a distribution is a "capital distribution," nor the special rule in subdivision (g) requiring an amount the fiduciary is in doubt about to be allocated to principal. This document does not classify any specific distribution received by a trust or determine how it should be allocated.

DEFAULT ALLOCATION OF RECEIPTS FROM MINERALS, WATER, OR OTHER NATURAL RESOURCES
UFIPA also sets a specific default allocation for receipts from an interest in minerals, water, or other natural resources that a trustee does not account for as a business. Probate Code § 16350(a) provides that, to that extent, the fiduciary allocates the receipt: to income, when received as delay rental or annual rent on a lease, as a factor for interest or its equivalent under an agreement creating a production payment, or on account of an interest in renewable water; to principal, if received from a production payment (except as just described); and between income and principal in a reasonable manner, when received on account of a nonrenewable water interest, as a royalty, shut-in-well payment, take-or-pay payment, or bonus, or from a working interest or any other interest not otherwise listed.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "To the extent a fiduciary does not account for a receipt from an interest in minerals, water, or other natural resources as a business under Section 16432, the fiduciary shall allocate the receipt in the following manner: (1) To income, to the extent received: (A) As delay rental or annual rent on a lease. (B) As a factor for interest or the equivalent of interest under an agreement creating a production payment. (C) On account of an interest in renewable water. (2) To principal, if received from a production payment, to the extent subparagraph (B) of paragraph (1) does not apply. (3) Between income and principal in a reasonable manner, to the extent received: (A) On account of an interest in nonrenewable water. (B) As a royalty, shut-in-well payment, take-or-pay payment, or bonus. (C) From a working interest or any other interest not provided for in subparagraph (A) or (B), or paragraph (1) or (2)."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 16350(a) (California Legislative Information text), the default allocation of receipts from an interest in minerals, water, or other natural resources (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=16350.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes only subdivision (a). Subdivision (c) creates a presumption that an allocation made under paragraph (3) of subdivision (a) (the between-income-and-principal category) is reasonable if the amount allocated to principal equals the federal depletion deduction allowed for the interest -- that presumption is not quoted or applied here. Subdivision (d) also gives a fiduciary who already held a minerals, water, or natural-resources interest before this chapter's January 1, 2024 effective date the option to keep allocating receipts from that pre-existing interest the way the fiduciary allocated them before that date, instead of using this section's default; this document does not determine whether that transition option applies to any specific interest held by a particular trust.

WHEN AN INCOME BENEFICIARY'S RIGHT TO NET INCOME BEGINS
UFIPA fixes the date an income interest begins, which determines from what point an income beneficiary's entitlement to net income is measured. Probate Code § 16375(a) provides that an income beneficiary is entitled to net income from the date the income interest begins, and that the interest begins on the date the trust specifies or, if none is specified, on the date an asset becomes subject to the trust for the current income beneficiary or to a successive interest for a successor beneficiary. Section 16375(b) fixes that date concretely: for an asset transferred to the trust during the settlor's life, the transfer date; and for an asset that becomes subject to the trust because of a decedent's death -- whether held directly by the trust or transferred to a fiduciary by a third party because of the death -- "on the date of the decedent's death, even if there is an intervening period of administration of the decedent's estate."

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "An income beneficiary is entitled to net income in accordance with the terms of the trust from the date an income interest begins. The income interest begins on the date specified in the terms of the trust or, if no date is specified, on the date an asset becomes subject to either of the following: (1) The trust for the current income beneficiary. (2) A successive interest for a successor beneficiary."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 16375(a) (California Legislative Information text), an income beneficiary's entitlement to net income from the date the income interest begins (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=16375.)
  "An asset becomes subject to a trust under paragraph (1) of subdivision (a) as follows: (1) For an asset that is transferred to the trust during the settlor’s life, on the date the asset is transferred. (2) For an asset that becomes subject to the trust because of a decedent’s death, on the date of the decedent’s death, even if there is an intervening period of administration of the decedent’s estate. (3) For an asset that is transferred to a fiduciary by a third party because of a decedent’s death, on the date of the decedent’s death."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 16375(b) (California Legislative Information text), the income interest's start date for an asset that becomes subject to the trust because of a decedent's death (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=16375.)
  Known gap: This clause addresses only when an income interest begins. It does not address the distinct question of when, and how, income is apportioned at the end of an income interest -- a related but separate set of rules in Probate Code §§ 16376-16377 (also in Article 7) that this document does not quote or describe. It also does not apply the beginning-date rule to determine the actual start date of any specific beneficiary's income entitlement under a particular trust.

citations.case: Cal. Prob. Code § 16327(b)-(c) (California Legislative Information text)
citations.cite: no duty to exercise or consider the power to adjust, and no liability for a good-faith choice either way
citations.quote: (b) This section does not create a duty to exercise or consider the power to adjust under subdivision (a) or to inform a beneficiary about the applicability of this section. (c) A fiduciary that in good faith exercises or fails to exercise the power to adjust under subdivision (a) is not liable to a person affected by the exercise or failure to exercise.

expectedJSON.gap: Subdivision (e) of § 16327 -- not quoted in this clause -- lists nine specific circumstances in which the power to adjust may not be exercised at all, including trusts that qualify for certain special tax benefits, interests payable as a fixed annuity or fixed fraction, permanent charitable set-asides, arrangements that would trigger federal income, estate, or gift tax consequences, a fiduciary who is not an "independent person," certain irrevocable trusts with a settlor income interest tied to public benefit eligibility, and a trust that is already a unitrust under Article 3. This document does not apply those restrictions, or the cofiduciary and delegation rules in subdivisions (f) through (h), to any specific trust or any specific adjustment; whether the power to adjust is available for a particular trust and a particular adjustment is not determined here.

expectedJSON.body: Separate from the power to adjust, UFIPA gives a trustee a power to change how a trust calculates the amount available to an income beneficiary in the first place. Probate Code § 16332(a) provides that a fiduciary, without court approval, by complying with the section's other requirements, may convert an income trust to a unitrust (so that net income becomes a fixed unitrust amount, typically a percentage of trust value, rather than actual income received), change the percentage or method used to calculate an existing unitrust amount, or convert a unitrust back to an income trust. Under § 16332(b), a fiduciary may take that action only if the fiduciary determines it will assist in administering the trust impartially, sends notice describing and proposing the action as required by § 16333, and no beneficiary objects within the applicable period; if a beneficiary does object, § 16332(c) allows the fiduciary or a beneficiary to ask the court to permit, modify, or prevent the proposed action.

citations.case: Cal. Prob. Code § 16332(a) (California Legislative Information text)
citations.cite: the fiduciary's power, without court approval, to convert an income trust to a unitrust, change a unitrust's calculation, or convert a unitrust back to an income trust
citations.quote: (a) A fiduciary, without court approval, by complying with subdivisions (b) and (f), may do any of the following: (1) Convert an income trust to a unitrust if the fiduciary creates in a record a unitrust plan for the trust providing for both of the following: (A) That in administering the trust, the net income of the trust will be a unitrust amount rather than net income determined without regard to this article. (B) The percentage and method used to calculate the unitrust amount. (2) Change the percentage or method used to calculate a unitrust amount for a unitrust if the fiduciary implements in a record a unitrust plan or an amendment or replacement of a unitrust plan providing changes in the percentage or method used to calculate the unitrust amount. (3) Convert a unitrust to an income trust if the fiduciary implements in a record a determination that, in administering the trust, the net income of the trust will be net income determined without regard to this article rather than a unitrust amount.

citations.case: Cal. Prob. Code § 16332(b)-(c) (California Legislative Information text)
citations.cite: conditions for taking the action -- an impartiality determination, notice, and the consequence of a beneficiary's objection
citations.quote: (b) A fiduciary may take an action under subdivision (a) if all of the following conditions are met: (1) The fiduciary determines that the action will assist the fiduciary to administer a trust impartially. (2) The fiduciary sends a notice in a record, in the manner required by Section 16333, describing and proposing to take the action. (3) No beneficiary objects to the proposed action in a writing delivered to the trustee within the period prescribed by subdivision (d) of Section 16502. (c) If a fiduciary receives, on or before the date stated in the notice under Section 16333, an objection in a record to a proposed action, the fiduciary or a beneficiary may request the court to have the proposed action taken as proposed, taken with modifications, or prevented.

expectedJSON.gap: This clause does not describe the detailed content requirements for a unitrust plan under §§ 16334-16338 (for example, the unitrust rate, the valuation method, or default provisions that apply if the plan is silent), nor the categories of trusts Probate Code § 16331(b) excludes from Article 3 entirely -- certain trusts tied to specific Internal Revenue Code provisions (26 U.S.C. §§ 170(f)(2)(B), 642(c)(5), 664(d), 2702(a)(3)(A)(ii)-(iii), or 2702(b)), such as certain charitable remainder and split-interest trusts. Whether a particular trust is eligible for unitrust conversion under this article, and what a specific unitrust plan for that trust should provide, is not addressed here.

expectedJSON.body: The notice a fiduciary must send before converting an income trust to a unitrust, changing a unitrust's calculation, or converting a unitrust back to an income trust has statutorily required contents. Probate Code § 16333 lists what the notice must include: the proposed action; for a conversion to a unitrust, a copy of the adopted unitrust plan; for a change in calculation, a copy of the amended or replacement plan; a statement that the recipient may object by stating the basis for the objection and delivering it to the fiduciary; the fiduciary's name and contact information; and the name and contact information of a person who can be contacted for more information. On timing, § 16333(e) requires the notice to state "[t]he date by which an objection under subdivision (d) shall be received by the fiduciary, which shall be at least 30 days after the date the notice is sent."

citations.case: Cal. Prob. Code § 16333 (California Legislative Information text)
citations.cite: the required contents of the notice of a proposed unitrust conversion or calculation change
citations.quote: A notice required by paragraph (2) of subdivision (b) of Section 16332 shall be sent as required by Chapter 5 (commencing with Section 16500), including notice to a beneficiary who is a minor and to the minor’s guardian, if any, and shall include all of the following: (a) The action proposed under paragraph (2) of subdivision (b) of Section 16332. (b) For a conversion of an income trust to a unitrust, a copy of the unitrust plan adopted under paragraph (1) of subdivision (a) of Section 16332. (c) For a change in the percentage or method used to calculate the unitrust amount, a copy of the unitrust plan or amendment or replacement of the unitrust plan adopted under paragraph (2) of subdivision (a) of Section 16332. (d) A statement that the person to which the notice is sent may object to the proposed action by stating in a record the basis for the objection and sending or delivering the record to the fiduciary. (e) The date by which an objection under subdivision (d) shall be received by the fiduciary, which shall be at least 30 days after the date the notice is sent.

expectedJSON.gap: This clause describes only the content requirements listed directly in § 16333; it does not describe the separate service mechanics referenced in that section -- § 16333 requires notice to be sent "as required by Chapter 5 (commencing with Section 16500), including notice to a beneficiary who is a minor and to the minor's guardian, if any" -- and this document does not quote or apply that Chapter 5 notice-service statute. Thirty days is a statutory floor, not a fixed deadline: a fiduciary may set a longer objection period, and this clause does not determine what objection period, if any, applies to a specific notice already sent for any particular trust.

expectedJSON.body: UFIPA sets a default rule for one of the most common receipts a trustee handles: a distribution from an entity in which the trust owns an interest, such as a corporation, partnership, limited liability company, regulated investment company, or real estate investment trust. Probate Code § 16340(c) provides the baseline: "Except as otherwise provided in paragraphs (2) to (4), inclusive, of subdivision (d), a fiduciary shall allocate money received in an entity distribution to income." Subdivision (d) then carves out categories that instead go to principal: property received that is not money; money received in exchange for part or all of the fiduciary's interest to the extent the distribution reduces that interest relative to other owners; money the fiduciary determines or estimates is a "capital distribution" (a return of capital or a total or partial liquidating distribution); and money from a regulated investment company or real estate investment trust that is a capital gain dividend, or comparably treated, for federal income tax purposes.

citations.case: Cal. Prob. Code § 16340(c) (California Legislative Information text)
citations.cite: the default rule allocating money received in an entity distribution to income
citations.quote: Except as otherwise provided in paragraphs (2) to (4), inclusive, of subdivision (d), a fiduciary shall allocate money received in an entity distribution to income.

citations.case: Cal. Prob. Code § 16340(d) (California Legislative Information text)
citations.cite: the categories of entity distributions allocated to principal instead
citations.quote: A fiduciary shall allocate to principal all of the following: (1) Property received in an entity distribution that is not money. (2) Money received in an entity distribution in an exchange for part or all of the fiduciary’s interest in the entity, to the extent the entity distribution reduces the fiduciary’s interest in the entity relative to the interests of other persons that own or hold interests in the entity. (3) Money received in an entity distribution that the fiduciary determines or estimates is a capital distribution. (4) Money received in an entity distribution from an entity that is a regulated investment company or real estate investment trust if the money received is a capital gain dividend for federal income tax purposes. (5) Money received in an entity distribution that is treated, for federal income purposes, comparably to the treatment described in paragraph (4).

expectedJSON.gap: This clause quotes only the baseline income/principal split in subdivisions (c) and (d); it does not quote or apply subdivisions (e) through (i), which set out the safe harbors, a 20%-of-fair-market-value threshold, and a multi-factor test a fiduciary may use to determine or estimate whether a distribution is a "capital distribution," nor the special rule in subdivision (g) requiring an amount the fiduciary is in doubt about to be allocated to principal. This document does not classify any specific distribution received by a trust or determine how it should be allocated.

expectedJSON.body: UFIPA also sets a specific default allocation for receipts from an interest in minerals, water, or other natural resources that a trustee does not account for as a business. Probate Code § 16350(a) provides that, to that extent, the fiduciary allocates the receipt: to income, when received as delay rental or annual rent on a lease, as a factor for interest or its equivalent under an agreement creating a production payment, or on account of an interest in renewable water; to principal, if received from a production payment (except as just described); and between income and principal in a reasonable manner, when received on account of a nonrenewable water interest, as a royalty, shut-in-well payment, take-or-pay payment, or bonus, or from a working interest or any other interest not otherwise listed.

citations.case: Cal. Prob. Code § 16350(a) (California Legislative Information text)
citations.cite: the default allocation of receipts from an interest in minerals, water, or other natural resources
citations.quote: To the extent a fiduciary does not account for a receipt from an interest in minerals, water, or other natural resources as a business under Section 16432, the fiduciary shall allocate the receipt in the following manner: (1) To income, to the extent received: (A) As delay rental or annual rent on a lease. (B) As a factor for interest or the equivalent of interest under an agreement creating a production payment. (C) On account of an interest in renewable water. (2) To principal, if received from a production payment, to the extent subparagraph (B) of paragraph (1) does not apply. (3) Between income and principal in a reasonable manner, to the extent received: (A) On account of an interest in nonrenewable water. (B) As a royalty, shut-in-well payment, take-or-pay payment, or bonus. (C) From a working interest or any other interest not provided for in subparagraph (A) or (B), or paragraph (1) or (2).

expectedJSON.gap: This clause quotes only subdivision (a). Subdivision (c) creates a presumption that an allocation made under paragraph (3) of subdivision (a) (the between-income-and-principal category) is reasonable if the amount allocated to principal equals the federal depletion deduction allowed for the interest -- that presumption is not quoted or applied here. Subdivision (d) also gives a fiduciary who already held a minerals, water, or natural-resources interest before this chapter's January 1, 2024 effective date the option to keep allocating receipts from that pre-existing interest the way the fiduciary allocated them before that date, instead of using this section's default; this document does not determine whether that transition option applies to any specific interest held by a particular trust.

expectedJSON.body: UFIPA fixes the date an income interest begins, which determines from what point an income beneficiary's entitlement to net income is measured. Probate Code § 16375(a) provides that an income beneficiary is entitled to net income from the date the income interest begins, and that the interest begins on the date the trust specifies or, if none is specified, on the date an asset becomes subject to the trust for the current income beneficiary or to a successive interest for a successor beneficiary. Section 16375(b) fixes that date concretely: for an asset transferred to the trust during the settlor's life, the transfer date; and for an asset that becomes subject to the trust because of a decedent's death -- whether held directly by the trust or transferred to a fiduciary by a third party because of the death -- "on the date of the decedent's death, even if there is an intervening period of administration of the decedent's estate."

citations.case: Cal. Prob. Code § 16375(a) (California Legislative Information text)
citations.cite: an income beneficiary's entitlement to net income from the date the income interest begins
citations.quote: An income beneficiary is entitled to net income in accordance with the terms of the trust from the date an income interest begins. The income interest begins on the date specified in the terms of the trust or, if no date is specified, on the date an asset becomes subject to either of the following: (1) The trust for the current income beneficiary. (2) A successive interest for a successor beneficiary.

citations.case: Cal. Prob. Code § 16375(b) (California Legislative Information text)
citations.cite: the income interest's start date for an asset that becomes subject to the trust because of a decedent's death
citations.quote: An asset becomes subject to a trust under paragraph (1) of subdivision (a) as follows: (1) For an asset that is transferred to the trust during the settlor’s life, on the date the asset is transferred. (2) For an asset that becomes subject to the trust because of a decedent’s death, on the date of the decedent’s death, even if there is an intervening period of administration of the decedent’s estate. (3) For an asset that is transferred to a fiduciary by a third party because of a decedent’s death, on the date of the decedent’s death.

expectedJSON.gap: This clause addresses only when an income interest begins. It does not address the distinct question of when, and how, income is apportioned at the end of an income interest -- a related but separate set of rules in Probate Code §§ 16376-16377 (also in Article 7) that this document does not quote or describe. It also does not apply the beginning-date rule to determine the actual start date of any specific beneficiary's income entitlement under a particular trust.
